title: Homes for Ukraine Share assurance and residual-custody public-record acquisition result
question: Does the currently available official record supply an independent Share migration assessment, residual former-supplier custody and deletion disposition, subject-level continuity or remedy case, independently reconciled cost and performance result, affected-party governance instrument, or successor-support and cloud-exit record sufficient to change the frozen Homes for Ukraine answer dimensions?

query_families: independent end-to-end Share migration assessment, source-to-destination reconciliation, incidents, rollback controls and auditor disposition
Palantir residual-custody inventory, deletion certificate, backups, derivatives, support copies and disaster-recovery disposition
subject-level Share cutover continuity, correction, deletion, complaint, remedy and follow-up
independent cost and service-performance reconciliation across the former platform, Made Tech support, cloud costs, staffing and incidents
affected-party governance authority and successor-support or cloud-exit capability

source_records.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government Digital
locators: MHCLG reports that it began building Share in summer 2024, migrated three years of operational data, delivered the service in September 2025, and exited the former supplier contract.

The account describes a phased migration with multiple rounds of quality assurance, but it does not publish source-to-destination counts, exception records, reconciliation results, continuity incidents, rollback evidence, or an independent auditor disposition.
The team states that it is preparing Share for a live service assessment later in 2026, so the article records assessment intent rather than a completed or published assessment result.

source_records.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
locators: The survey asks local-authority users to report problems with the test migration from Foundry to Share, including data that is completely missing, data that is incorrect, and functional problems caused by the observed behaviour.
Respondents are instructed not to include personal identifiable information and may request a follow-up research call when person-level detail is required to explain an issue.

The published survey establishes an official migration-defect intake route, but it does not publish the responses, defect denominator, reconciliation results, corrective actions, closure decision, or independent assurance.

source_records.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
locators: The survey asks users for thoughts and questions about the transition from Foundry to the new Share Homes for Ukraine data system.
Technical problems are routed to Jira and users may submit more than one response, establishing a continuing transition-feedback mechanism.
The published page does not disclose the responses, incident classes, correction ledger, user-level outcomes, migration sign-off, or independent disposition.

source_records.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government and Home Office
locators: MHCLG and the Home Office are controllers for the scheme, Made Tech assists with the MHCLG-owned Share platform, and the platform is hosted on cloud infrastructure in London.
Jira enquiries are triaged by XBP, with personal information normally removed before forwarding while exceptions remain possible when a guest cannot be located on Share.

The notice publishes access, rectification, erasure, objection, and complaint routes, but it does not publish an observed Share cutover case joining one person to continuity, correction, deletion, remedy, and follow-up.
The decision concerns a request to the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham for information about the Homes for Ukraine initiative, including an audit report of the local programme.
The Commissioner held that the public interest favoured disclosure of portions of the audit report while permitting other portions to remain withheld under section 36.

The record concerns a local authority programme audit and does not establish central Share migration assurance, Palantir residual-custody reconciliation, a deletion certificate, or a subject-level Share remedy; transfer to those claims is prohibited.

source_records.authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government Digital
locators: The account identifies Share as the replacement for the old platform and records continued work by the Homes for Ukraine digital and policy teams after launch.
The team reviewed prior local-authority research transcripts and conducted stakeholder work to select the service name, while noting that the system is not public facing.

The article supports continuing operation and design activity, but it does not supply migration reconciliation, residual-custody disposition, independent cost or performance assurance, affected-party governance authority, or a remedy outcome.

route_ledger.preserved_reason: The departmental account establishes delivery, phased quality assurance, supplier exit and continued operation, but it does not publish an independent migration packet or completed service-assessment result.

route_ledger.query_family: missing data, incorrect data, functional defects, reconciliation, corrective action and closure
route_ledger.preserved_reason: The survey proves that migration defects were solicited from users but publishes no response set, denominator, reconciliation, corrective-action ledger, sign-off or independent assurance.

route_ledger.surface: Homes for Ukraine system change survey
route_ledger.query_family: transition questions, technical incidents, Jira handling and user outcome
route_ledger.preserved_reason: The route establishes transition feedback and technical escalation, but it does not publish the incident ledger, correction outcome, migration sign-off or user-level remedy.

route_ledger.query_family: current processors, hosting, residual dependencies, access, rectification, erasure, complaint and observed remedy
route_ledger.preserved_reason: The notice identifies Made Tech, London cloud infrastructure, Jira and XBP and publishes rights routes, but it supplies no observed continuity, correction, deletion or remedy case tied to the Share transition.

route_ledger.query_family: audit disclosure, programme control findings and transfer to central Share assurance
route_ledger.preserved_reason: The decision opens access to portions of a local programme audit but does not establish the central platform migration, former-supplier custody, deletion, cost, performance or subject-remedy claims.

route_ledger.surface: GOV.UK service-standard and service-assessment publication search
route_ledger.query_family: Share Homes for Ukraine live service assessment report and expert-peer disposition
route_ledger.preserved_reason: The bounded official search located operational guidance and the departmental statement that an assessment was planned, but no published Share assessment report; this is not a claim of nonexistence or exhaustive search.

route_ledger.query_family: Made Tech support contract, Palantir deletion, residual-copy inventory, backup disposition, cloud exit and successor procurement
route_ledger.preserved_reason: The bounded procurement search did not locate an exact public object satisfying the custody, deletion, support-exit or cloud-exit receipt; no current-public-nonexistence inference is authorized.

route_ledger.surface: Share service naming and continuing design account
route_ledger.query_family: continued operation, user research, affected-party governance and reusable public capacity
route_ledger.preserved_reason: The account supports continued public-team activity and stakeholder research, but it does not grant affected people authority over material decisions or prove independent operation, remedy or durability.

next_required_receipts: A published independent end-to-end Share migration-assurance packet joining source and destination counts, exceptions, reconciliation, continuity incidents, rollback controls and auditor disposition.
A residual Palantir custody inventory and deletion certificate covering production, backup, derivative, support and disaster-recovery copies.
A source-addressed person-level Share cutover case joining continuity, access, correction or deletion request, authority, remedy and follow-up.
An independently reconciled cost and service-performance denominator covering former-platform costs, Made Tech support, cloud costs, incidents, staffing and claimed savings.
A binding affected-party governance instrument and a tested successor-support or cloud-exit record.

assessment.evidence_tier: Official departmental delivery and operating records, official user-research intake surfaces, a central privacy notice, an ICO adjudicative record, bounded official publication and procurement search, and immutable repository custody.
assessment.venue: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, GOV.UK, Citizen Space, the Information Commissioner's Office, the public procurement record, the M-05 implementation frontier, and issue 345.
assessment.target: Independent Share migration assurance, residual former-supplier custody and deletion, subject-level remedy, independently reconciled value and performance, affected-party governance, and successor or cloud exit.
assessment.upside: The record fixes the delivery claim, migration-defect and transition-feedback channels, current processors and hosting, rights routes, adjacent audit access, and continued service activity into one reproducible acquisition ledger.
assessment.downside: No located public object supplies the migration reconciliation, residual-custody disposition, deletion certificate, observed subject remedy, independent cost and performance result, affected-party authority, or successor-exit proof required by the frontier.
assessment.failure_mode: Treating delivery, phased quality assurance, surveys, official savings claims, privacy rights, local-program audit access, public code, or continued operation as independent assurance, complete custody reconciliation, remedy, governance, or durability.
